items.description: Runtime lifecycle validation rejects a cancelled spike.
items.analysis: The cancel lifecycle declares generic transitions from defined and spiking to cancelled, but spike validation currently derives statuses only from explicitly spike-scoped transitions. A cancelled spike would therefore be invalid.
items.recommendation: Allow generic terminal cancellation for a spike without admitting unrelated planning or implementation statuses, and add a regression test.
items.rationale: Confirmed defect: cancellation explicitly accepts spikes, so a cancelled spike must validate.

items.description: Cancelling one member of a reciprocal concurrent-delivery pair leaves the surviving record invalid.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-2; independently confirmed in src/specle/lifecycle.py and the reciprocal relationship contract.
items.analysis: Concurrent-delivery relationships are explicit reciprocal records rather than dependencies. Archiving only one member leaves the other pointing to a missing active record and blocks validation and delivery.
items.recommendation: Detect only an explicit reciprocal concurrent-delivery partner, require confirmation, then remove only that reciprocal relationship from the surviving active record in the same recoverable mutation.
items.rationale: Preserve one-target cancellation while requiring an explicit, confirmed unlink of the known surviving partner; do not infer or cancel additional work.

items.description: Runtime validation permits cancelled records without their required archive location or timestamp.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-3; independently confirmed in src/specle/lifecycle.py and the cancellation requirements.
items.analysis: The shared schema keeps lifecycle timestamps optional, so runtime lifecycle validation must enforce cancellation-specific evidence and location. It currently permits active cancelled records and archived cancelled records without cancelled_at.
items.recommendation: Require cancelled_at for cancelled records, reject cancelled records outside the archive, derive terminal acceptance through the existing helper, and add focused negative tests.
items.rationale: The requirements explicitly define both invariants, and validating them keeps interrupted cancellation mutations visible.

items.description: Cancellation guidance ambiguously forbids selected targets and omits direct-delivery consequences.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-4; independently confirmed in the cancel and commit skill guidance.
items.analysis: The target must be explicit, not inferred from the selector, but an explicitly named selected target is valid. Direct/local delivery has recorded branch and commit evidence without a PR, which also requires user-directed handling.
items.recommendation: Clarify explicit-name selection, surface direct/local delivery evidence before cancellation, and stop the dependency scan before mutation when an active status record is unreadable or malformed.
items.rationale: These corrections preserve the intended user-directed handling of selected and already delivered work.

items.description: Adjacent lifecycle guidance still treats complete as the sole terminal archive outcome.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-5; independently confirmed in the lifecycle policy and activate and explain skills.
items.analysis: A worktree-local selector can remain after another worktree archives its target as cancelled. Guidance must treat that archived target as terminal and replaceable, while read-only explanation must cover both terminal outcomes.
items.recommendation: Synchronise blueprint and installed policy, activate, and explain guidance for cancelled selector cleanup, replacement, updated_at, and archival inspection.
items.rationale: This prevents a stale local selector from blocking future activation and completes the documented terminal-state model.

items.description: Regression tests omit broad cancellation workflow-guidance assertions.
items.analysis: The accepted runtime defects need focused executable coverage, but the proposed remaining tests would repeatedly test agent-executed Markdown workflow prose and simulate cancellation scenarios in the regular suite.
items.recommendation: Add broad packaged-skill and guidance-contract tests.
items.rationale: Keep the suite focused on executable runtime and schema invariants; agent-guidance scenarios are verified directly rather than through recurring workflow simulation.

items.description: The review record uses findings instead of the established items collection.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-7; independently confirmed in src/specle/lifecycle.py and docs/LAYOUT.md.
items.analysis: Resolved-review validation reads items. Retaining findings would make a later resolved review invalid despite an otherwise valid record.
items.recommendation: Use the established items collection while preserving all current source records and dispositions.
items.rationale: The review record must use the documented collection consumed by runtime validation.
